target.title: feat(policy): check authored message routing
target.body:
Closes #111050

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where operators could not express or continuously verify message-routing intent in the Policy plugin. A stale binding channel id, empty binding set, or unexpected fallback could silently route inbound messages to the default agent while `policy check` remained clean.

## Why This Change Was Made

This adds opt-in routing conformance to the bundled Policy plugin without changing core config validation, gateway startup, runtime routing, or fallback behavior. Operators author structural requirements and representative route probes in `policy.jsonc`; Policy evaluates those probes with OpenClaw's public runtime resolver.

Routing evidence is deliberately redacted. It records binding indexes and channel ids plus each authored probe's id, resolved agent, and match kind. It does not serialize peer, account, guild, team, role, session, or binding-destination identifiers. Routing findings are review-required and never automatically rewrite bindings.

## User Impact

Operators can now require at least one route binding, reject bindings whose channel is absent from configured `channels.*`, and assert that representative inbound routes resolve to an expected agent at an expected binding specificity.

Existing policies are unchanged unless they add a `routing` section. Policies without routing retain the same evidence shape and attestation hashes.

## Evidence

Exact before/after proof ran in the dedicated `openclaw-dev-gw` checkout with identical synthetic fixtures and isolated state under `~/.openclaw-dev/proofs`. Channels were disabled. No production config, gateway, LaunchAgent, or live message traffic was touched.

- Before: merge base `8853217ec72f3b3c357da18ad6b519510f1cfce6`
- After: PR head `0a8460a8f603625ff91fe9c2e503ae470ab7e78d`
- Dev gateway proof port: `19001`; production port `18789` was not used

| Scenario | Exact merge base | PR head |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Retired `bluebubbles` binding, `config validate --json` | Valid; binding is not rejected | Still valid by design; this PR is Policy-only |
| Retired binding, `agents bindings --json` | Binding is listed as present | Unchanged runtime listing behavior |
| Routing policy present | `policy/policy-jsonc-invalid`: `routing` is unsupported | Routing policy is supported |
| Healthy peer binding and fallback | Cannot express the invariant | Policy clean |
| Empty bindings | Cannot express the invariant | `routing-bindings-required`, `routing-agent-mismatch`, `routing-match-kind-mismatch` |
| Retired `bluebubbles` binding | Silently accepted by config validation | `routing-binding-channel-unconfigured` naming `bluebubbles`, plus probe mismatch findings |
| Privileged default fallback | Cannot express the intended destination | `routing-agent-mismatch` and `routing-match-kind-mismatch` |
| Empty bindings, no routing policy | Clean; attestation `sha256:91a6fb99f643e0400a641208e947639e5197ba07657a1f6c91374fa1588bf67f` | Clean with the same attestation hash |

Runtime proof on PR head:

- `doctor --lint --json` emitted the same three retired-binding findings as `policy check --json`.
- The healthy fixture started the built Gateway on `127.0.0.1:19001` with the Policy plugin loaded, reached `gateway ready`, and returned a clean concurrent `policy check --json` result.
- The dev Gateway then shut down cleanly and port `19001` was confirmed idle.
- `policy check --json` emitted no seeded peer or group identifiers.

Additional verification:

- 357 focused Policy tests passed, including CLI compare, Doctor registration, schema, evidence privacy, and all four incident fixtures.
- `tsgo:extensions`, `tsgo:extensions:test`, and `lint:extensions` passed using the trusted-source local fallback after the delegated Testbox wrapper duplicated dispatches.
- `git diff --check` passed.
- Codex autoreview was run repeatedly and all accepted findings were fixed. Its final scoped-routing claim was rejected because scoped policy validation explicitly disallows `routing`, routing metadata declares no scope selectors, and the scoped docs table excludes it.
